versions.changelog:
No changes detected in this version (1.0.5); content remains the same as the previous release.

- No file changes were made.
- No new features, fixes, or documentation updates in this release.

**Summary: Major update to analysis workflow, adds principles and new reference guides.**

- Enforces code-driven data analysis: all data from GSC/GA4/PSI must be processed via Python scripts, not manual reading.
- Expands core principles and workflow: adds site reconnaissance, clear phase-based checklist, and new requirements for chart generation and report writing.
- Refines data storage and environment setup: updates directory structure, emphasizes virtual environment usage with `uv`, and details config file locations.
- Adds new reference guides: introduces documentation for data collection, visualization, website reconnaissance, user personas, and reporting.
- Removes Bing and GA4 API reference files to focus on goal-oriented methodology with new documentation.
- Adds utility and configuration scripts under `scripts/`, supporting modular, reproducible analysis.

**Goal-driven data analysis and charting update:**

- Shifted to a goal-first workflow: First understand website goals and intended user journeys, then analyze data to measure if user behavior matches these goals.
- Added strong separation of raw data (`data/`), analysis outputs (`analysis/`), and chart images (`charts/`) for clear project organization.
- Introduced standardized Python/matplotlib chart generation for every quantitative analysis step, with strict requirements for chart-first reporting and visual consistency.
- Formally defined which charts must be generated in each analysis phase, including specific types/insights for SEO, traffic, journey, and funnel analysis.
- Added detailed chart type selection guide and chart embedding conventions for Markdown reports.
- Prepared new scripts and guides for funnel and Bing analysis (see added references and script files), expanding analytical capabilities.

- Added three new audit scripts: geo_audit.py, perf_audit.py, and seo_audit.py for enhanced SEO, Performance, and GEO analysis.
- Introduced an SEO & GEO optimization checklist (references/SEO-GEO-Optimization-Checklist.md) for comprehensive best-practice auditing.
- Updated the workflow to include a new Phase 5b: SEO & GEO optimization checklist audit.

google-analytics-and-search-improve v1.0.1 changelog

- Updated documentation to improve clarity and structure in English.
- Added a `configs/` directory to the recommended data storage layout.
- Replaced all Chinese-language sections and user prompts with English equivalents.
- No functional or code changes; workflow and audit instructions remain the same.
- Improved formatting and notes for configuration, user workflows, and directory structure.

Initial release of the google-analytics-and-search-improve skill.

- Analyze website data via Google Search Console API and GA4 Data API, with options for API auto-collection, manual CSV import, or browser-only audit.
- Audit live sites with browser automation; capture screenshots and performance metrics using PageSpeed Insights.
- Review project source code if provided, checking for SEO, performance, content, UX, conversion, and technical issues.
- Generate data-driven improvement plans covering top optimization opportunities across six key dimensions.
- Store all data, logs, and temporary files in a dedicated, user-isolated directory, separated from code.
